faqs.a: Beautify (pretty-print) adds indentation and line breaks so humans can read the structure. Minify removes all unnecessary whitespace so the payload is as small as possible for transfer.
faqs.q: What is the difference between beautify and minify?

faqs.a: Yes. Both operations parse the JSON first, and any syntax error is reported with its line and column before output is produced.

json-formatter.formula:
pretty:  JSON.stringify(value, null, gap)     // gap = 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tab
minify:  JSON.stringify(value)                 // no whitespace at all
sort:    recursively reorder object keys A-Z before stringifying
Note: JSON numbers, strings, booleans, null, arrays, and objects are the only valid values.
howTo: Paste your JSON into the input box - minified, messy, or broken.
Pick an indent style: 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tab. Optionally enable sort keys.
Click Beautify for readable output or Minify for the smallest possible payload.
If the JSON is invalid, read the reported line and column, fix it, and the output updates live.
Copy the result or download it as a .json file.
keyFacts: JSON Formatter parses, validates, beautifies, and minifies JSON documents.
Beautify adds indentation and line breaks; minify strips all unnecessary whitespace.
Syntax errors are reported with line and column numbers derived from the parser position.
Optional key sorting reorders object keys alphabetically at every level without changing values.
Statistics show total bytes, total key count, and maximum nesting depth.
Formatting is lossless: values are never modified, only whitespace and key order.
json-formatter.keywords: json formatter, json beautifier, json minifier, format json online, json pretty print, validate json
limitations: Only strict JSON is accepted: trailing commas, comments, single quotes, and unquoted keys are errors.
Duplicate object keys are silently resolved by the parser (last value wins) - see JSON Validator to detect them.
Extremely deep or huge documents may be slow; formatting runs on the main thread.
Number precision follows JavaScript doubles: very long numbers may lose precision when parsed.
